Bitcoin Core Contributor Finds $0.35 Attack Could Link Bitcoin Addresses to Node IPs

Bitcoin Core contributor Abubakar Sadiq Ismail disclosed on Delving Bitcoin that a long-known privacy weakness in Bitcoin Core’s wallet rebroadcast mechanism could allow attackers to link Bitcoin addresses to the IP addresses of nodes tracking them for less than $0.35 per attempt. The method achieved a 100% success rate across 30 simulated attributions on a regression test network (regtest), but has not been validated on mainnet. The weakness affects both hot and watch-only wallets, meaning an identified node does not necessarily control the associated funds. Other potentially affected software includes Bitcoin Knots, Sparrow in Bitcoin Core mode, Specter Desktop, Liana and Electrum Personal Server. Disabling wallet broadcasting can mitigate the risk but requires users to broadcast their transactions manually. A proposed code change, PR #36482, remains unreleased and does not eliminate all rebroadcast-related privacy risks. — link

BNB Chain released a new L1 litepaper targeting high-frequency trading, payments, private finance, and autonomous AI agents. It will run alongside BNB Smart Chain, retaining BNB as its native token without issuing a new one.

The EVM-compatible L1 separates transaction ordering and execution, uses SubBlocks for preliminary ordering feedback, and reserves block capacity for payments and other designated transactions. Native account abstraction supports passkeys, transaction batching, revocable permissions, and gas sponsorship. Private settlement supports BNB and eligible BEP-20 tokens, alongside partially public application interactions.

A public testnet is in development, parallel EVM execution is planned, and TEE-based ordering protection remains a proposal. — link

Hong Kong-Based Market Maker Auros, Which Survived the FTX Collapse, Is Gradually Winding Down Operations

According to CoinDesk, citing two sources familiar with the matter, Hong Kong-based crypto market maker Auros is gradually winding down operations. The reasons and timeline remain unclear, and the firm has not responded to requests for comment.

Founded in 2019, Auros estimated it handled around 4% of global crypto exchange trading volume, according to co-founder and CIO Ben Roth in July 2024. After FTX’s collapse in 2022 left some of its assets trapped, Auros entered court-supervised restructuring in the British Virgin Islands before exiting provisional liquidation in March 2023 following a $17 million funding round led by Vivienne Court, with participation from Bit Digital.

Auros later invested in projects including Pyth and Berachain and launched Aurora, an institutional trading portal connecting centralized and decentralized markets, in September 2026. — link

Net amount of the cash dividend will be reinvested after applicable withholding taxes, fees, costs, and other deductions, into additional units or fractions of the same underlying security. Eligible users will receive dividends in the form of WENB, NVDAB, QCOMB, PYPLB and WDCB bStocks respectively.
